text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A plan to decentralise Kenya Cooperative Creameries looks set to continue following endorsement of the move by the ruling Kenya African National Union (KANU) party parliamentary group.
- The government dismisses as outrageous and exaggerated a Kenya Human Rights Commission report on prisons conditions.
- President Daniel arap Moi accuses some embassies of inciting the public against the government.
- Ruling KANU party warns against careless talk, saying action will be taken against leaders responsible for statements that spark tribal animosity or bring disunity to the party.
- World Food Programme officials say that food for starving refugees is being sold in local markets.
- Armed gangsters brazenly terrorise parts of Nairobi city and shoot at a victim of a robbery three days after Police Commissioner Shedrach Kiruki declared "total war" on violent criminals.
- A total of 37 international companies and eight foreign governments are among this year's exhibitors at the Nairobi International Show.
- An Eldoret church leader reveals that some churches are attempting to promote anarchy in the country using opposition parties and asks Kenyans to be aware of these evil.
